decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a small, growing niche where demand is still uncertain and holding the option costs little, so it stays open even though its web presence shrank to a mention in 2019.
Small volume ionization chambers are core dosimetry items with long lifecycles and steady demand from small-field and stereotactic QA, and keeping them costs little.
This chamber fits the firm's established calibration and dosimetry portfolio, which shows its value is being realized, so a further commitment is justified.
Standard clinical chambers are reference instruments that customers buy repeatedly over decades, so there is no reason to abandon this one.
Relative dosimetry chambers pair with the firm's water phantoms and scanning systems, giving stable value at low upkeep cost.
Thimble chambers are mainstream QA devices with steady demand, and keeping this one costs the firm little.
